description: END-ACCEPT explicit scope terminator (ISO §2023:14.9.1.2: `ACCEPT identifier-1 [ FROM mnemonic-name-1 ] [ END-ACCEPT ]` and the other ACCEPT formats) - a COBOL-2002 introduction. THE EDGE IS QUOTED from the edition texts (kb/Work PB3965): the ANSI X3.23-1985 ACCEPT formats are `ACCEPT identifier-1 [ FROM mnemonic-name-1 ]` and `ACCEPT identifier-2 FROM { DATE | DAY | DAY-OF-WEEK | TIME }` (§1985:VI.6.5.2), with no terminator, and §1985:IV.4.4.4 'The explicit scope terminators are the following' lists END-ADD, END-CALL, END-COMPUTE, END-DELETE, END-DIVIDE, END-EVALUATE, END-IF, END-MULTIPLY, END-PERFORM, END-READ, END-RECEIVE, END-RETURN, END-REWRITE, END-SEARCH, END-START, END-STRING, END-SUBTRACT, END-UNSTRING and END-WRITE; §2002:14.8.1.1 prints `ACCEPT identifier-1 [ FROM mnemonic-name-1 ] [ END-ACCEPT ]`, and §2002:14.4 Table 13 pairs `ACCEPT | [NOT] ON EXCEPTION | END-ACCEPT`, the conditional phrase of the screen ACCEPT 2002 adds (§2002:F.2 item 1: 'The ACCEPT statement is extended to allow a screen item specified in the screen section to be used for operator input at a terminal'). §2014:14.9.1.1 prints the 2002 format unchanged, so 2014 = 2023. The gate is COBOL0816 through ConstructRegistry.Check; kb/Work PB134 made the terminator parse, so the gate and the matrix assertions are live.
